We provide safe and equitable care, for every stage of life, delivered with world-leading expertise and over 175 years of experience.

Liaise with vendor regarding issues.












Publish training and manual for resources for user community.












Create and manage users' accounts and security rights.

Professional and customer focused communications via both the Central ticket management system and phone.












Maintain and adhere to operational procedures and complete appropriate support documentation when procedures change.












Develop and maintain a customer focused culture and contribute to a friendly and co-operative working environment, fostering strong working relationships with all colleagues to deliver quality outcomes.












Build and leverage relationships internally with Digital and Information Division teams such as Service Desk, Infrastructure, Desktop Experience, and Support Services.












Participate in ad hoc projects as directed by Director of Application Services.












Other duties as assigned from time to time by the Head of Partner Applications.









About You






Qualifications, registrations and licences:









Bachelor's degree in computer science, IT, or a related field preferred.












Prior experience in a system administrator role or similar.










Technical skills, knowledge and experience: 









Excellent verbal-written communication and documentation skills.












A strong desire and capability to listen, analyse and recommend.












Excellent interpersonal and relationship building skills.












Excellent time and personnel management skills.












Ability to work within deadlines.












Ability to work unsupervised.












Experience with clinical communication systems or healthcare IT. 






Good knowledge of Microsoft 365 platform and Teams functionality








For a confidential discussion and to explore this opportunity further, please reach out to Liz Feeny - Head of Partner Applications on 0412 032 226.

Our Culture and Values 






At Monash Health, our people are at the heart of everything we do. Our culture is inclusive, supportive and future-focused, underpinned by clear values and a commitment to continuous improvement. 






Our teams play a critical role in bringing our new strategy to life, challenging traditional approaches, embracing innovation, and ensuring every appointment reflects our commitment to equity, transparency and excellence. 






You'll be encouraged to share ideas, contribute to improvement initiatives, and grow alongside experienced professionals who are passionate about what they do. 






We are Full Hearted, Open Minded and All In, enabling excellent service delivery and a positive candidate and employee experience every time. 






We recognise the value of equal employment opportunity. We are committed to patient safety, promoting fairness, equity and diversity in the workplace and to Child Safe Standards.

Applications are accepted via the Monash Health online EHub system. For information including how to apply and probity check requirements, please click here for the 'Application Guide'


Applications will be screened upon receipt and selection activity may commence prior to the closing date.

Do you want to earn some extra income, while fitting around your current commitments? Do you enjoy shopping and love great customer service? Have a keen eye for detail and excellent communication skills? You might be just who we are looking for to join our team of Professional Mystery Shoppers.

No matter your background, current commitments or experience, you can help businesses measure and improve their customer service, by pretending to be a customer and reporting on the experience. Our detailed instructions ensure you are supported to know what to look out for and how to succeed. We regularly engage with clients from a wide range of industries, like retail, beauty services, cafes and fast food, pharmacies, vet clinics and many more, with assignments available all around Australia.

Skills & Tech Needed:
- Exceptional communication skills, both verbal and written English
- Keen observation skills and a sharp memory
- Access to a computer (or laptop/tablet), email, and reliable internet
- A smartphone for capturing photos as proof of visit
- Ability to manage deadlines and communicate effectively when things change
- Strong ability to follow instructions, then ask for help when necessary

We pride ourselves on the fastest Mystery Shopping payments in the country, with deposits processed weekly into your nominated bank account. No gift vouchers, points or working for free, and if a purchase is required, you get reimbursed and get to keep it! Compensation varies for each assignment, generally ranging from $20 to $50, sometimes more, for onsite visits and $15 to $30 for phone calls. All of this information is available before you apply for each assignment. 

You can apply for as many jobs each month according to your schedule, but it’s important to understand that this role is very casual and we recommend signing up to multiple mystery shopping providers to increase your chance to pick up assignments. 

If you want more information, head to our website for informative blogs and links to our social sites, as well as testimonials from Mystery Shoppers and clients alike. https://abovebenchmark.com.au/mystery-shopping-jobs/

The next step to joining our team is to apply from our confidential application form: https://abovebenchmark.com.au/mystery-shopper-application/

We look forward to hearing from you.

Do you want to make a meaningful difference in the lives of people experiencing mental illness? At Central Coast Local Health District (CCLHD), we are committed to Trusted Care, Better Health for Everyone, and we are looking for compassionate Registered Nurses to join our Mental Health team.

About the Opportunity

As a Registered Nurse in Mental Health, you will be an integral member of a multidisciplinary team, delivering high-quality, recovery-oriented care to consumers across a range of mental health settings. You will provide person-centred nursing care, support positive health outcomes, and contribute to creating a safe, therapeutic environment for consumers and their families.

This position plays a key role in supporting consumers on their recovery journey while promoting quality, safety, and continuity of care. In this role you will:

Deliver comprehensive mental health assessments, including risk assessment and management, to support consumers in achieving their recovery goals. 

Plan, implement, coordinate, and evaluate evidence-based nursing care to promote positive health and wellbeing outcomes. 

Accurately document and maintain healthcare information in relevant electronic systems to support safe, effective, and legally compliant care. 

Collaborate with consumers, families, carers, and the multidisciplinary team to provide person-centred, trauma-informed, and recovery-focused care.

For more information about this role, please view the Position Description.

About You

We are looking for someone who has:

Current Authority to Practice as a Registered Nurse with the Australian Health Practitioner Regulation Agency (AHPRA). 

Recent postgraduate clinical experience in mental health with a commitment to evidence-based practice and continuous quality improvement. 

Strong verbal, written, interpersonal, and clinical communication skills, including the effective use of information technology. 

Demonstrated ability to work collaboratively within a multidisciplinary team while maintaining professional and ethical boundaries. 

A commitment to recovery-oriented, consumer-focused, and trauma-informed care that values the involvement of families and carers. 

Excellent organisational skills with the ability to prioritise workload, adapt to changing environments, and demonstrate resilience, integrity, and accountability.

Applicants must have current work rights in Australia or be a permanent resident or citizen. Unfortunately, we cannot consider applicants who do not meet this requirement.

Clear Communication. Better Understanding. Stronger Outcomes

Exceptional written communication skills with proven ability to produce plain-language, accessible content.


Strong project management, stakeholder engagement, and facilitation skills.


Experience in education-coaching and building capability in others.


High level of digital literacy and attention to detail.











Highly regarded









Formal training or certification in health literacy or plain language.


Postgraduate qualification in a relevant field.


Experience in co-design, consumer engagement, or quality improvement.


Knowledge of accessibility standards and cultural safety practices.

At Monash Health we embrace diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive workplace where everyone can contribute their best.









Work for an organisation that truly values patient voices and is committed to equitable, person-centred care.


Be part of a supportive, innovative Patient Experience team that is making tangible improvements every day.


Access to professional development, including health literacy and co-design opportunities.


Generous salary packaging, employee benefits, and work-life balance options.


Contribute to a purpose-driven organisation with a clear Strategy 2026-2031 focused on excellence and innovation.
